# UNITY001 asset-missing-meta

A tracked file or folder under `Assets/` (or an embedded package under `Packages/`) has no tracked `.meta`.

## What it does

With the opt-in `unity` pack enabled, every git-tracked asset and every folder that holds one needs a tracked `<asset>.meta` beside it. Names Unity ignores (a leading dot, a trailing `~`, `cvs`, a `.tmp` extension), `Packages/manifest.json` and `packages-lock.json`, and the `Assets` and package root folders are exempt. Untracked files never count. The finding names the asset.

## Why it matters

Without the `.meta`, each clone invents a new guid for the asset and every scene or prefab reference to it breaks.

## Remedy

Open the project in the editor so Unity writes the `.meta`, then commit it with the asset.

## Examples

### A violating case fires

```csharp expect=fire file=Assets/Hero.cs
public class Hero { } // warn: UNITY001
```

### A conforming case is clean

```csharp expect=clean file=Assets/.hidden.cs
public class Hidden { }
```
